## Data

Download both data files from this Google Drive folder: **[https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1mVoWddGN_f0kiWmDOpdibV9Rrdx6yxfo?usp=sharing](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1mVoWddGN_f0kiWmDOpdibV9Rrdx6yxfo?usp=sharing)**

Place both files in the **same folder** as this `.Rmd` before knitting.

### Dataset 1 — World Happiness (Problem 1)

`happiness.csv` contains country-level data from the **World Happiness Report**, an annual survey that ranks countries by self-reported well-being. Respondents rate their own lives on the **Cantril ladder** — a 0–10 scale where higher scores reflect greater life satisfaction. The dataset includes one observation per country (most recent available year) with two variables:

- `log_gdp`: log GDP per capita (natural log of GDP per person in international dollars)
- `happiness`: average Cantril ladder score (0–10 scale)

```{r load-happiness}
happy <- read.csv("happiness.csv")
```

### Dataset 2 — NOAA Global Surface Temperature Anomalies (Problem 2)

`noaa_temp.csv` contains annual global surface temperature data from the **National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA)**. Each observation is a yearly average of land and ocean temperature anomalies — the departure (in °C) from the 20th-century baseline average (1901–2000). Positive values indicate a warmer-than-average year; negative values indicate a cooler-than-average year. The dataset covers 1960–2023 with three variables:

- `year`: calendar year
- `anomaly`: mean annual temperature departure from the 20th-century average (°C)
- `year_c`: year centered at 1960 (i.e., `year - 1960`), used as the predictor so the intercept has a meaningful interpretation

```{r load-temp}
temp <- read.csv("noaa_temp.csv")
```
